title: Pete Bread (Pon Dulce) Made by Hand: Enriched Dough from Start to Finish
summary: In this America’s Test Kitchen video, Artisan Brian Ford demonstrates making Pete bread—a silky, buttery, enriched loaf referenced from Pon Dulce Pon Dulce—entirely by hand and compares it to a mixer approach. The hosts cover weighing ingredients (vs. volume), choosing yeast (fresh vs. instant/dry) with a quick conversion, and managing hydration for enriched dough by reserving water and gradually adding fats. The demonstration then shifts from mixer to hand kneading, showing how to incorporate butter while developing gluten, followed by a 5-minute rest, shaping into rounds and a pan loaf, and two proofing stages. The bake is done at 375°F with an egg wash, and doneness is discussed via color and internal temperature around 200°F. The video includes tasting and sandwich-building ideas to illustrate the bread’s tender, springy crumb. Throughout, the dialog emphasizes technique over guesswork, with practical tips on dough texture, timing, and shaping for a well-formed loaf.
topics: Yeast types: fresh vs instant vs active dry
Reserving water to control dough consistency
Gradual water and fat incorporation during mixing
Mixing methods: stand mixer vs hand mixing
Dough rest and smoothing between steps
Dividing and shaping dough (rounds and pan loaf)
Shaping technique: palm vs fingertip work
Proofing: first and second rise and skin prevention
Doneness cues: color and internal temperature ~200°F
Sandwich and serving ideas with Pete bread
